newsitem.title: USA: Dow ends shy of new record, indices hit peaks.
newsitem.headline: Dow ends shy of new record, indices hit peaks.

text.p: Blue-chip stocks rose Monday but fell short of a new all-time closing high as technology shares hit a late sell-off, but other indices snared records amid window-dressing at the end of the quarter.

"We got some pressure across the tech sector with some profit-taking. There's some concern now that window-dressing has come to a conclusion and there may be some earnings disappointments in tech-land," said Bill Meehan, a Prudential Securities market analyst.
The Dow Jones industrial average rose 9.25 points to 5,882.17. The blue chip index earlier hit a session peak of 5,907.32, topping Sept. 23's record high finish of 5,894.74.
In the broader market, advancing issues led declines 1,295 to 1,069 on heavy volume of 388 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
The Standard & Poor's index of 500 stocks scored a new record, up 1.14 to 687.33, surpassing Sept. 20's all-time closing high of 687.02.
The NYSE Composite index added 1.06 to 367.33, eclipsing Friday's record peak of 366.27. The average price per share rose 11 cents.
The Nasdaq Composite index lost 3.13 to 1,226.92 after earlier rising nearly four points.
Among technology stocks, Dow component IBM Corp., which was up 2-1/4 earlier, fell 1/4 to 124-1/2. Intel lost 1-7/16 to 95-7/16 and 3Com was off 2-1/16 to 60-1/16.
Oppenheimer chief investment strategist Michael Metz said last-minute window-dressing helped prop up stocks.

"Everybody who has a cosmetic approach to portfolios wants to be fully exposed to rising equities," Metz said. "In addition, there's the increasing conviction of no Fed (credit) tightening in the foreseeable future."

The bond market erased an early advance and turned lower after the Commerce Department said August single-family homes sales jumped 4.7 percent to an annual rate of 832,000 units -- the highest rate in more than a decade.
July homes sales were revised up to 795,000 units from the strong 783,000 units first reported.
The benchmark 30-year Treasury bond fell 7/32, raising the yield to 6.92 percent from 6.91 percent at Friday's close.

As expected, the Chicago Purchasing Managers group reported that its index slipped to 56.3 in September from a strong 60.0 in August. An index below 50 signals a slowing manufacturing economy, while a reading above 50 suggests expansion.
In another report, the federal government said August personal income and consumer spending each rose 0.6 percent, both in line with estimates.
While home sales pressured bonds, analysts said equity investors were relieved to see signs of economic strength that will aid corporate profits.
William LeFevre, a senior market analyst at Ehrenkrantz King Nussbaum, noted the market had fared well in the third quarter, with the Dow up 4 percent.
"The notice this quarter was the big cap stocks. When they survived the (July) decimation of the techs, it gave added life to this market," he said.
Among special situations, Kmart surged one to 10-1/4 after Morgan Stanley upgraded it to strong buy from outperform.
AT&T Corp. rose 3/4 to 52-1/4 and Lucent Technologies added 2-1/4 to 45-7/8. AT&T began distributing to shareholders the 525 million Lucent shares it holds, finalising its spin-off of Lucent.

ADT Ltd. lost 3/4 to 19-1/8 and Republic Industries rose 1-3/4 to 29 after they agreed to terminate their merger pact. The value of the stock transaction, originally pegged at $5 billion, has declined sharply since it was announced in July. Lehman Brothers upgraded ADT to buy from outperform.

Ford added 5/8 to 31-1/4. UAW members at Ford overwhelmingly approved a new three-year labour contract with the company. The contract guarantees jobs for 95 percent of Ford's current workforce of 105,000. The pact gives workers a $2,000 lump sum payment in the first year, followed by 3 percent base wage hikes in the second and third years.

The vote came one day after the UAW and Chrysler reached a tentative agreement patterned after the economic terms of the Ford deal. Chrysler added 5/8 to 28-5/8. GM, which is still negotiating a new pact, added 3/4 to 48.
The American Stock Exchange index rose 3.02 to 571.49.
The Wilshire Associates Equity Index -- the market value of NYSE, American and Nasdaq issues -- was 6,765.649, up 11.321 or 0.17 percent.
